title: Ctrl-C recorded as task failure
grade_detail: patch_apply: git apply failed: error: b/runner.py: No such file or directory; fuzzy: no hunks applied (skipped=['runner.py@19'])

answer.patch:
--- a/runner.py
+++ b/runner.py
@@ -19,3 +19,3 @@
         try:
             row = run_one(task)
-        except BaseException as e:   # noqa: BLE001
+        except Exception as e:
             row = {
answer.reason: KeyboardInterrupt inherits from BaseException, not Exception. The bare BaseException catch was intercepting Ctrl-C, recording a failure row, and persisting it to disk instead of letting the signal propagate to terminate the process cleanly. Switching to Exception allows KeyboardInterrupt (and SystemExit) to bubble up while still catching normal task errors.

title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: The timeout handler only returned a CompletedProcess when stdout had content. If the child wrote only to stderr before timing out, the condition failed and raised ProcTimeout, dropping the stderr diagnostics. Added an or-check for stderr to ensure the CompletedProcess is returned whenever either stream has output.

title: Warmup ignores short timeout

answer.patch:
--- a/warmup.py
+++ b/warmup.py
@@ -11,2 +11,1 @@ def warmup(model: str) -> dict[str, Any]:

-     return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK")
+     return chat(model, "Reply with exactly: OK", timeout_s=config.DEFAULT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S)
